title: fix(cluster): an object authored during a store outage is served by every replica after its resync
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi926TiHxhsZMVATUkqxg2xD2)_

Fixes #31722

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

Measured on the diff: one new public method,
`ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.resyncMetadataMutationPubSub()`, and its
result type `MetadataMutationResyncReport`, exported from
`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. Nothing is removed or made required. The
claim read `no`; the measurement says `yes (widening)`, as it did for #31721.
No metadata an author writes changes.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：多副本集群中，Redis 等共享存储断线期间在 A 副本上新建、修改或删除的对象，B 副本在自己的集群驱动重连（`cluster.resync`）后会自动收敛，不再需要重启。
- 为什么改：`metadata.mutated` 通道（让其他副本注册新对象的那条）是唯一没有重同步入口的通道；断线期间丢失的提示会让其他副本一直回答 `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`（或旧定义、或已删除的对象），直到重启。
- 风险与回滚：单节点（默认内存驱动）完全不变，从不触发；重同步只读本副本自己的 `sys_metadata`，读失败时不删除任何注册项。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- 先看：`metadata-protocol` 的新文件 `protocol-mutation-resync.ts`（选哪些项重新收敛），以及 `service-cluster` 的 `metadata-cluster-bridge-plugin.ts`（注册一行）。
- 两分钟验证：`cd packages/runtime && pnpm exec vitest run src/cluster-metadata-mutation-resync.integration.test.ts`，两个内核共享一个 SQLite 文件和一条会丢消息的总线。
- 需要你做的：无。

## What changes

- **Lane 2 has a resync seam (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`).**
  `resyncMetadataMutationPubSub()` reads `sys_metadata`'s active rows once,
  with only their address and `checksum` and never a body. It then
  re-converges each item a lost hint could have touched:
  - a row whose checksum moved since this replica last converged on it (a lost
    save or publish);
  - an item this replica converged on that has no active row now (a lost
    delete);
  - an item a hint or a local write named since the last convergence (a revert
    brings an earlier checksum back, so the checksum alone cannot tell).

  Each item goes through `applyRemoteMetadataMutation`, the applier a
  delivered hint runs, from this replica's own re-read. Nothing travels on the
  wire. A row that is gone takes the delivered delete's heal walk.
- **The baseline.** `attachMetadataMutationPubSub` seeds a per-replica ledger
  with one active-row read. Every convergence keeps the ledger current. Hints
  and local writes mark items. Resyncs run one at a time, and an item touched
  during a resync stays marked. With no baseline (the seed read failed), the
  first resync re-converges every active row.
- **A read that fails is never a delete.**
  - If the active-row read fails, the resync rejects and changes nothing.
  - If one item's re-read fails, that item is kept as this replica holds it and
    stays marked for the next resync. The failures are logged once per resync
    (`console.error`, with the items and the first cause).
- **The bridge calls it (`@objectstack/service-cluster`).**
  `MetadataClusterBridgePlugin` registers lane 2 through `registerLaneResync`
  on the same `cluster.resync` event as lanes 1, 3, 4 (#31721) and 5 (#31597). A protocol
  that predates the seam is skipped, and a rejected resync is a warning, as
  for the other lanes.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx` §6.2 and the bridge docblock now
  describe lane 2's resync instead of "Lane 2 has no resync yet".

## Why

#31721 left the `metadata.mutated` lane as the one lane without a resync. Its
hint is what makes a peer re-run the ObjectQL registry write-through. So a hint
lost during a store outage left every other replica answering
`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` for an object authored meanwhile (or serving its old body,
or serving it after a delete) until restart.

### Step 0: full re-convergence vs a diff

Measured on a booted showcase (`bootShowcase`, `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=object`),
with N objects authored and the lane attached:

| N | Diff, nothing lost | Diff, 5 changed | Full re-apply of every row | Listener replays (full) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 50 | ~1 ms, 50 unchanged | 12 ms, 5 converged | 97 ms | 50 |
| 300 | 2 ms, 300 unchanged | 9 ms, 5 converged | 406 ms | 300 |

The address-and-checksum read takes ~1 ms at both sizes. These are
shared-box timings, so read them as ratios.

**Choice: the diff.** A full re-apply costs one delivered-hint convergence per
stored row on every reconnect. Each convergence also replays the item into
the local mutation listeners, and some of those re-sync a whole family per
event (authored hooks and actions). So the cost grows with the catalog even
when nothing was lost. A since-timestamp re-read was ruled out:
- a hard delete leaves no active row to carry a timestamp;
- the writers' clocks are not this replica's.

### A finding from the measurement

On the booted showcase, the first build's resync and seed reads were refused
with `PermissionDeniedError` (a read under a context that carries no
principal). Every resync would have failed on a secured stack. Both reads now
carry `context: { isSystem: true }`, as the repository's own reads do. The
fan-out harness now refuses a principal-less column-subset read, as the
secured engine does, so this is pinned (A8a/A8b below). The two-kernel test
has no security plugin, so it could not catch it.

## Tests

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.cluster-mutation-fanout.test.ts`:
  a new `[#31722] cluster.resync` describe with 10 cases. The shared harness
  gains a read fault (every read, or item re-reads only), the registered
  labels, and the principal-less refusal:
  - ⭐ an object authored while the hint was lost is served after the resync;
  - a lost update re-converges that item only, and an unchanged item is not
    re-applied;
  - a lost delete takes the heal walk;
  - a delete of a row present at attach is found from the baseline;
  - a revert to an earlier checksum after a delivered hint;
  - a local write on the peer is re-read;
  - a failed active-row read rejects and keeps every entry;
  - an item whose re-read fails is kept, logged once, and retried;
  - CONTROL: nothing lost means nothing is re-applied;
  - CONTROL: with no transport, the seam does nothing.
- `packages/services/service-cluster/src/metadata-cluster-bridge-plugin.test.ts`:
  - the existing resync cases now assert lane 2 and the info line;
  - 2 new cases: a protocol that predates the seam, and a rejected protocol
    resync is a warning.
- `packages/runtime/src/cluster-metadata-mutation-resync.integration.test.ts`
  (new): two `LiteKernel`s over one SQLite file, a lossy bus, a `test-bus`
  driver with liveness, and the real bridge.
  - ⭐ author on A with the hint lost. B does not know the object. B's
    `cluster.resync` runs. B serves the object and its row.
  - CONTROL: a delivered hint converges B with no resync.
  - CONTROL: on the `memory` driver, the seam is never called (R3: the
    in-process driver never emits `cluster.resync`).

### Ablations

Each was run against the tests above, first on the pre-merge head and again
on the merged head. All went red both times, and each restore left the file
equal to HEAD.

| # | Mutation | Red |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | bridge lane-2 registration removed | 3 bridge cases; the runtime ⭐ through the built `dist` |
| A2 | active-row read failure swallowed (rows = []) | the failed-read case |
| A3 | a failed item re-read drops its key | the item-failure case |
| A4 | no unchanged skip | 2 |
| A5 | the hint's touch removed | 4 |
| A6 | lane-2 resync registered before the in-process guard | 4 (the memory CONTROL included) |
| A7 | the local write's touch removed | the local-write case |
| A8a | the seed read without the system context | the baseline-delete case |
| A8b | the resync read without the system context | 9 |

The A1 runtime leg uses a preflight marker that is present in the pristine
`dist`, absent under the mutation, and present after the restore.

## Acceptance notes

- Delete semantics follow the delivered-hint path, because it is the same
  applier. A per-item re-read failure is logged and kept, not deleted.
- The seed read runs once per attach, only where the bridge attaches (a driver
  that crosses a process boundary).
- R3 holds: the `memory` driver never emits `cluster.resync`, and the bridge
  never attaches lane 2 on it.
- Landing order: #31597 (PR #31785, the settings lane) edited the same bridge
  file and §6.2 and landed first. `main` is merged in after it (a merge
  commit). Lane 5 stays at `kernel:bootstrapped` with `subscribeResync()` in
  both phases; lane 2 registers at `kernel:ready` like lanes 1 to 4.

## Verification

- Per touched package, `pnpm typecheck` and package-scoped lint (root eslint
  on the directory, `--no-inline-config`) exit 0. A full `vitest run`:

  | Package | Test files | Tests |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | metadata-protocol | 329 passed, 4 skipped | 22607 passed, 26 skipped |
  | service-cluster | 11 | 158 |
  | runtime | 568 | 10424 passed, 19 skipped |

- All of the above ran on the merged head `70a46315`.
- `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` was derived on `70a46315` and gave 104
  commands. Each was run (all exit 0) and reconciled with `--ran`: 104
  derived, 104 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. `check-nul-bytes` exits 0.
- Forced test edits: none. The existing bridge resync cases gained lane 2 in
  their assertions, and the fan-out suite's shared harness was extended.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (`packages/spec` untouched.)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: n/a.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
